newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan begins test run of second advanced reactor.
newsitem.headline: Japan begins test run of second advanced reactor.

text.p: Tokyo Electric Power Co Inc, Japan's biggest power utility, said on Tuesday it had started trial operations of its second advanced boiling water reactor.
The reactor, located at the utility's Kashiwazaki Kariba nuclear power complex on the Sea of Japan coast, has a capacity of 1.36 million kilowatts (kw), a company statement said.

Advanced reactors are safer and more economical than the conventional type, Tokyo Electric said, adding that one of the key features is that the reactor's coolant recirculation pump is installed inside the pressure vessel of the reactor, instead of outside.
Commercial operations of the nuclear reactor, the seventh at the complex, are due to start in July 1997, it said.
That will make the Kashiwazaki Kariba complex the world's largest nuclear power complex with a capacity of 8.21 million kw, Tokyo Electric said.
Currently, a 7.28 million kw nuclear power complex in Ontario, Canada, is the world's largest.
Tokyo Electric started commercial operations of its first advanced boiling water reactor at the Kashiwazaki Kariba complex in November.
Japan relies on nuclear power for about 33 percent of its electricity needs.
